purpose: Cephalexin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as skin infections, ear infections, urinary tract infections, and throat infections like strep throat. It only works against bacteria, so it will not help with colds, the flu, or other viral infections. Your doctor prescribed it because they believe bacteria are causing your infection.
how_it_works: Cephalexin works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria cells. Without this protective wall, the bacteria cannot survive and they die off. Think of it like punching holes in a bacteria's armor so your immune system can finish the job.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, and stomach cramps. Some people may notice a mild skin rash. Taking this medication with food can help reduce stomach upset. If you have severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody, contact your doctor right away.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin antibiotics, because there is a small chance you could also react to cephalexin. Seek emergency help immediately if you develop hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, as this could be a serious allergic reaction. Always finish your full course of antibiotics even if you feel better, to prevent the infection from coming back or becoming resistant. Let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth every 6 to 12 hours, depending on the type and severity of your infection. Most courses of treatment last 7 to 14 days. Always follow the exact directions on your prescription label and try to take doses at evenly spaced times each day.
